texts.preamble: Muhammed Salih vs State Of Kerala on 14 March, 2016 Author: B.Sudheendra Kumar Bench: B.Sudheendra Kumar In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr. Justice B.Sudheendra Kumar Monday, The 14Th Day Of March 2016/24Th Phalguna, 1937 Crl.Rev.Pet.No. 2093 of 2013 () -------------------------------- Crl.A 25/2012 of Addl. D.C. & Sessions Court - Ii, Kasaragod Cc 382/2009 of J.M.F.C.-Ii,Hosdrug Revision Petitioner(S)/Revision Petitioner/2Nd Accused: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Muhammed Salih, Aged 37 Years S/O.Abdulla Haji, A K Store, D No Xii-483 Bekal Junction, Pallikkara P O, Kasaragod Dist By Advs.Sri.M.Ramesh Chander (Sr.) Smt.Dennis Varghese Respondent/Respondent: --------------------------------------- State Of Kerala Rep By Public Prosecutor, High Court Of Kerala Ernakulam-682031 By Public Prosecutor, Shri.V.S.Sreejith This Criminal Revision Petition Having Been Finally Heard On 14-03-2016, The Court On The Same Day Passed The Following: B.Sudheendra Kumar, J. - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -- - - -- - - - - - - - - - -- - - - - - - - - Crl.R.P. No.2093 of 2013 - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - Dated this the 14th day of March 2016 Muhammed Salih vs State Of Kerala on 14 March, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98578931/ 1 O R D E R
texts.facts: The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 26.9.2006, PW1, the Food Inspector, purchased 400 gram of Raggi from the shop of the first accused. After sampling as per rules , one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst. The Public Analyst filed Ext. P11 report stating that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for the food item under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 and therefore, the same was adulterated. Thereafter, on the request of the accused, the second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis. Ext.P20 certificate of the Central Food Laboratory would show that the sample contained synthetic yellow colour F.C.F. and carmoisine and therefore, it did not conform to the standard prescribed for food item and hence, it was adulterated. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW4 were examined and Exts. P1 to P27 were marked for the prosecution. No evidence was adduced on the side of the revision petitioner.
texts.arguments: 5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P20 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument. 6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act. Therefore, Ext. P20 certificate of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra). It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal. In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Muhammed Salih vs State Of Kerala on 14 March, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98578931/ 2 Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused. The matter was referred to a Division Bench and the Division Bench also affirmed the said decision, submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
